questions.question: Comprehension:Read the following passage and answer the questions given below-In 1947, when India gained independence, a young man named Verghese Kurien arrived in Anand, Gujarat, to manage a government creamery. Though trained as a mechanical engineer, Kurien was deeply moved by the struggles of local dairy farmers, who were exploited by middlemen. What began as a temporary posting soon turned into a lifelong mission. Kurien collaborated with Tribhuvandas Patel, a local leader, and together they transformed small village cooperatives into a thriving movement—later known as Operation Flood, or more popularly, the White Revolution.Through innovation and collective effort, the project modernized dairy production, ensuring that profits returned directly to the farmers. Under Kurien’s leadership, India evolved from a milk-deficient country to the world’s largest producer of milk. Beyond its economic success, the revolution symbolized self-reliance and empowerment in rural India. Kurien’s unwavering belief that development must come “from the people, for the people” reshaped the nation’s agricultural landscape and inspired generations to believe that sustainable change begins with local initiative and shared responsibility.Even today, Amul, the cooperative he helped build, stands as a testament to how visionary leadership and grassroots collaboration can transform an entire economy. Kurien’s story is not merely about milk; it is about dignity, innovation, and the power of collective determination.What motivated Kurien to stay in Anand?
options: The success of the local cooperative
His desire to earn a higher salary
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (The exploitation of dairy farmers) है।
